title: TARP capital injection on bank risk-taking

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
Difference-in-differences (DID) comparing TARP recipients (treated) vs non-recipients (control) before and after TARP implementation. The key identifying assumption is parallel trends: absent TARP, treated and control banks would have followed similar trajectories in non-performing loan ratios. This is plausible given both groups are regulated banks subject to similar macroeconomic conditions during the financial crisis.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(fixest)
library(ggplot2)

# Read the data
data <- read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s04_data.csv")

# Convert variables to appropriate types
data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    unit_id = as.factor(unit_id),
    period = as.integer(period),
    treated = as.integer(treated),
    post = as.integer(post)
  )

# Main DID regression with unit and time fixed effects
did_model <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, data = data)

# Print main result
cat("=== MAIN DID RESULTS ===\n")
print(summary(did_model))
cat("\nTARP Effect on Non-Performing Loan Ratio:", round(coef(did_model)["treat_x_post"], 4), "\n")

# Parallel trends test - interact treated with each pre-period
# Create relative time periods (normalize post=1 periods as 0, 1, etc.)
data <- data %>%
  arrange(unit_id, period) %>%
  group_by(unit_id) %>%
  mutate(
    first_post_period = min(period[post == 1]),
    rel_period = period - first_post_period
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Create event study with leads and lags
# Exclude rel_period = -1 as base period
event_study <- feols(y ~ i(rel_period, treated, ref = -1) | unit_id + period, 
                     data = data)

cat("\n=== EVENT STUDY / PARALLEL TRENDS TEST ===\n")
print(summary(event_study))

# Test joint significance of pre-treatment coefficients
pre_treatment_coefs <- grep("rel_period::-[2-9]", names(coef(event_study)), value = TRUE)
if(length(pre_treatment_coefs) > 0) {
  pre_test <- wald(event_study, pre_treatment_coefs)
  cat("\nPre-treatment parallel trends test (H0: all pre-coeffs = 0):\n")
  cat("F-statistic:", round(pre_test$stat, 3), "p-value:", round(pre_test$p, 3), "\n")
}

# Robustness check 1: Without unit fixed effects (pooled regression)
did_pooled <- feols(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post | period, data = data)
cat("\n=== ROBUSTNESS: WITHOUT UNIT FIXED EFFECTS ===\n")
cat("TARP Effect:", round(coef(did_pooled)["treat_x_post"], 4), "\n")

# Robustness check 2: Clustered standard errors by unit
did_cluster <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, 
                     data = data, cluster = "unit_id")
cat("\n=== ROBUSTNESS: CLUSTERED STANDARD ERRORS ===\n")
cat("TARP Effect (clustered SE):", round(coef(did_cluster)["treat_x_post"], 4), "\n")

# Summary statistics by group and period
cat("\n=== SUMMARY STATISTICS ===\n")
summary_stats <- data %>%
  group_by(treated, post) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_npl = round(mean(y, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
    sd_npl = round(sd(y, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
    n = n(),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )
print(summary_stats)

# Calculate raw difference-in-differences
raw_did <- summary_stats %>%
  mutate(group = ifelse(treated == 1, "Treated", "Control"),
         period_label = ifelse(post == 1, "Post", "Pre")) %>%
  select(group, period_label, mean_npl) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = period_label, values_from = mean_npl) %>%
  mutate(difference = Post - Pre)

cat("\nRaw Difference-in-Differences:\n")
print(raw_did)
cat("DID Estimate:", round(raw_did$difference[raw_did$group == "Treated"] - 
                         raw_did$difference[raw_did$group == "Control"], 4), "\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a positive coefficient on the TARP interaction term (treat_x_post), indicating that TARP recipients increased their non-performing loan ratios relative to non-recipients after receiving capital injections. The magnitude should be economically meaningful, perhaps 0.1-0.3 percentage points, reflecting moral hazard effects where government capital support reduced banks' incentives for prudent lending. However, the effect might be smaller or even negative if TARP came with enhanced regulatory oversight that disciplined risk-taking behavior.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: DID — treated=TARP recipients, control=non-recipients; parallel pre-trends required
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: TARP banks show higher NPL ratios post-injection, consistent with moral hazard
_ground_truth.main_effect: 20bp increase in NPL ratio for TARP banks
